caption: Network Scan Info
description: The Network Scan Info object describes metadata about a network scan job, including the scan technique, duration, completion status, the scanner source endpoint, and any operational flags.
name: network_scan_info

flags.description: A list of scanner-specific operational flags for the network scan job, such as service_detection, os_detection, or aggressive_timing. The primary scan technique should be captured in type_id.

scan_duration.description: The time span of the network scan job, including start time, end time, and total duration.

scanner_endpoint.description: The network endpoint of the scanner source that executed the scan probes.

status_id.description: The normalized completion status of the network scan job.

0.caption: Unknown
0.description: The network scan completion status is unknown.

1.caption: Completed
1.description: The network scan completed successfully and all targets were probed.

2.caption: Partial
2.description: The network scan completed but only a subset of targets were probed.

3.caption: Failed
3.description: The network scan failed and no usable results were produced.

99.caption: Other
99.description: The network scan status is not mapped. See the status attribute, which contains a data source specific value.

type.description: The network scan technique, normalized to the caption of the type_id value. In the case of 'Other', it is defined by the scanner.

type_id.description: The normalized identifier of the network scan technique used.

1.caption: TCP SYN
1.description: A half-open TCP SYN scan that sends a SYN packet and checks for a SYN-ACK response without completing the handshake.

2.caption: TCP Connect
2.description: A full TCP connect scan that completes the three-way handshake to determine port reachability.

3.caption: UDP
3.description: A UDP scan that sends UDP packets and infers port state from ICMP responses or lack thereof.

4.caption: TCP ACK
4.description: A TCP ACK scan used to map firewall rulesets by determining whether ports are filtered.

5.caption: TCP FIN
5.description: A TCP FIN scan that sends FIN packets to probe ports, exploiting a subtlety in the TCP RFC to distinguish open from closed ports.

6.caption: TCP NULL
6.description: A TCP NULL scan that sends packets with no TCP flags set to probe ports.

7.caption: TCP XMAS
7.description: A TCP XMAS scan that sends packets with FIN, PSH, and URG flags set to probe ports.

99.caption: Other
99.description: The scan technique is not mapped. See the type attribute, which contains a data source specific value.
